title: Prices up, rate?

predict.q: The price level rises by 10%. The central bank keeps the money supply at 600. What happens to the nominal interest rate?

options.s: It rises, because the money supply shifts left.
options.fb: The price level changes money demand; the money supply is set by the central bank.

options.s: It falls, because people have more money.
options.fb: Higher prices mean people need more money for the same purchases, so demand for money rises.

options.s: It rises, because money demand shifts right.
options.fb: People need more money for the same real purchases: MD shifts right and the rate rises from 4% to 4.5%.

options.s: It stays at 4%, because the central bank has not acted.
options.fb: A shift in MD moves the rate even with no central bank action.

task: Move the price level slider to 110 and watch MD and the rate. Then move the money supply slider.

target.do: Move the price level slider to 110 (money supply 600), then press Check.

takeaway: A higher price level raises money demand, so with a fixed money supply the nominal rate rises.
